title: Second difference: obligation—works-covenant exacts all; grace-covenant still binds toward perfection
source_text: XXXIX. Secundo peccata ista inter se differre dicit ratione obligationis, qua ad ea vitanda obligamur. Ad cujus rei intelligentiam, notat primo foedus operum, sive legem praecise sumptam, obligare ad omnia & singula legis praecepta perfecte, quoad omnes particulas, conditiones, & circumstantias exactae obedientiae, servanda: & proinde ad vitanda omnia, etiam levissima peccata; idque stricte & praecise, sub peri-culo & poena aeternae damnationis. Secundo, foedus gratiae non simpliciter tollere obligationem legis qua nos ad omnes gradus, conditiones, & circumstantias perfectae obedientiae praestandas, & per consequens ad omnia, etiam levissima peccata fugienda obligat. Quoniam adhuc tenemur ad perfectionem illam, quantum in nobis est, eniti atque aspirare, & serio dolere quod ab ea deficiamus, ejusque rei veniam quotidianis a Deo precibus implorare.
pass_a_gloss: Secondly he says those sins differ among themselves by reason of the obligation by which we are bound to avoid them. For understanding this matter he notes first that the covenant of works, or the law precisely taken, binds to keeping all and each of the law’s precepts perfectly as to all particles, conditions, and circumstances of exact obedience: and therefore to avoiding all, even the lightest sins; and that strictly and precisely, under peril and penalty of eternal damnation. Secondly, that the covenant of grace does not simply take away the law’s obligation by which it binds us to performing all degrees, conditions, and circumstances of perfect obedience, and consequently to fleeing all, even the lightest sins. Since we are still bound to strive and aspire after that perfection as much as in us lies, and seriously to grieve that we fall short of it, and daily to implore pardon for that from God by prayers.
pass_b_english: Works-covenant: strict, precise duty to shun even the lightest fault under eternal peril.
Grace-covenant does not erase that aim—it still obliges striving, grieving shortfall, and daily plea for pardon.

choices.why: Grace softens rigor without abolishing the law’s demand.
